messages.author: d2bffd1a5d780ca8
messages.subject: Error message in measurement invariance
parts:
Hello, guys.

I am trying to evaluate partial metric invariance using the "measurementInvariance" argument. My group has only two levels (males and females), but when I run the code I get this error message:

Error in measurementInvariance(model = my_model, data = my_data, group.partial = "sex"): Well, the number of groups is 1. Measurement invariance across 'groups' cannot be done.

Any suggestions?

Thanks.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Error message in measurement invariance
parts: I am trying to evaluate partial metric invariance using the "measurementInvariance" argument.

The measurementInvariance() function is only designed to evaluate different levels of full invariance (i.e., all loadings, all intercepts, etc.).  There is a partialInvariance() function that provides post hoc tests for individual items.
Error in measurementInvariance(model = my_model, data = my_data, group.partial = "sex")

There is no group.partial= argument to the measurementInvariance() function.  It can be passed to lavaan(), but see the ?lavOptions help page for the description of how to actually use it (it accepts parameters, not the name of a grouping variable).  I think you mean to set group="sex", which would resolve the error of having only 1 group (because you did not correctly provide a grouping variable).

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

Hello Professor Terrence Jorgensen,

As I mentioned in a previous post, I need to perform an analysis of measurement invariance on a second-order model. I have already reviewed in detail the two papers you recommended and the help content for the measEq.syntax function. However, I have some difficulties.

When I evaluate the weak or metric invariance through the measEq.syntax function and set the factor loadings constraint using the group.equal = "loadings" argument, I get a result in which all coefficients are equal, not just the lambda, but also beta ones.

I suspect the above is not appropriate. As I understood it, it’s advisable to first test the invariance of the factor loadings in the first-order factors, and then do it in the second-order ones. I also think I understand that to do this with the measEq.syntax function, I must first use the "loadings" argument and then the "regressions" argument.

The same thing happens when I try to evaluate scalar or strong invariance. As recommended by Chen, Sousa and West (2005), first the equivalence must be analyzed by restricting the intercepts of the observed variables, and then testing this same level of invariance, but adding the intercepts of the latent variables. However, when I use the argument group.equal = c (“loadings”, “intercepts”), once again, all intercepts are equal.

I would like to know how I can constrain only one type of parameter at a time; that is, first restrict only the factor loadings, leaving the regression coefficients to be freely estimated, and then restrict both parameters. And the same with the intercepts, but also with the residual variance and the disturbance.

How can I fix this problem? I have tried modifying the syntax that the measEq.syntax function generates but not succeeded. I have a hard time understanding how the syntax works. On the other hand, would it be correct to compare the models in which factor loadings and regression coefficients are restricted at the same time with the previous configural model? Can I proceed in this way with the other levels of invariance?

Here are my codes and results

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Error message in measurement invariance
parts: When I evaluate the weak or metric invariance through the measEq.syntax function and set the factor loadings constraint using the group.equal = "loadings" argument, I get a result in which all coefficients are equal, not just the lambda, but also beta ones.

No, your syntax doesn't do that.  Your syntax doesn't even know that there are multiple groups, because you supplied the group= argument without supplying the data= in which to find it.  So measEq.syntax() returned syntax for a siingle-group model, which is why you only see one label and one value (or NA) for each parameter.  You can supply data, or you can at least pass a vector of sample sizes to indicate the number of groups (see below), although that second option is only available in the development version.

Because your syntax has only one label per parameter, lavaan recycles that label for all groups, so all parameters (not just loadings) are constrained to equality.  But measEq.syntax() will return correct syntax for separately constrained first- and second-order loadings if it knows there are multiple groups.  Here is a reproducible example:

HS.higher <- '
visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9
intel   =~ visual + textual + speed
'
syntax.hi <- measEq.syntax(configural.model = HS.higher,
                           sample.nobs = c(1,1), # two indicate 2 groups without data
                           group.equal = "loadings")
cat(as.character(syntax.hi))
summary(syntax.hi)

Notice that the higher-order loadings will have the same parameter label except for the ".g1" or ".g2" suffix for different groups.

Glad my function is helping to execute the methods you read about,

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Error message in measurement invariance
parts: What arguments should I use to constrain the disturbances associated to the second-order factors? As far as I know, the residuals argument allows to constrain the residual variance of measured variables, but what option do I use in the case of latent variables?

"lv.variances" will constrain variances of all latent variables, both residual variances of latent indicators and exogenous variances of higher-order factors.  You can use the group.partial= argument to free the higher-order factor variance, in order to constrain only the residual variances of first-order indicators.  I noted this strategy with respect to latent intercepts in the help-page Details: "To test equivalence of lower-order and higher-order intercepts/means in separate steps, the user can either manually edit their generated syntax or conscientiously exploit the group.partial or long.partial arguments as necessary", in case that also becomes relevant for you.

How do I get the test for the difference in the robust chi-squared statistics?  When I use the anova or compareFit option, the results are based in the standard statistics, but I need the robust scaled version from Satorra-Bentler.

If you requested it when fitting the model (either using estimator = "MLM" or test = "satorra.bentler"), then the difference between (naive) chi-squared statistics will be scaled using the S-B method.  This should be stated explicitly at the top of the anova() output, which also appears at the top of the nested-model comparisons part of the compareFit() output.  Here are details about how the robust chi-squared difference test is calculated:

https://www.statmodel.com/chidiff.shtml

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

Question 1

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Error message in measurement invariance
parts:
can I constrain both parameters at the same time? by analyzing the sequence “configural, thresholds and loadings, intercepts, residuals”?


Yes.  In fact, you can only separately test thresholds if your indicators have 4 or more categories.

Question 2

This question is related to the previous one. I’m currently evaluating measurement invariance in three different psychometric scales. By doing so, I get findings that I don't understand and I don't know if these results are due to an error from my part. Specifically, in one scale the degrees of freedom (and all the fit indexes) from the configural model and the model with thresholds constrained are exactly the same. Nonetheless, this doesn’t happen when comparing the configural and thresholds constrained models in the two other inventories. Is this normal? Is it something that can happen or is it due to an error?
If your indicators for that scale have 3 categories, the threshold-invariant model is equivalent to any configural model.  See the Wu & Estabrook article from the help-page References.

Question 3

When declaring the data as categorical using the argument ordered in measEq.syntax function, is it necessary to declare again the data as categorical in cfa command from lavaan?
Yes, unless the data are already of class "ordered" in the data.frame.

Question 4

When declaring the data as categorical using the argument ordered in measEq.syntax function, I must omit the estimator argument to avoid error messages or using both commands produce no errors? What do you suggest?
I don't quite understand, but WLSMV is the default estimator when any indicators are declared as ordered.  You don't need to specify the estimator argument at all.

Question 5

How can I compare the latent variable means between groups (i.e. countries, sex, race) using multigroup confirmatory factor analysis? Do you have any tutorial for lavaan?

No, but once the thresholds, loadings, and intercepts are constrained to equality across groups, then latent means are estimable (except the first group's is usually fixed to 0 for identification) and therefore comparable.  To test their equality, you can use lavTestWald() or fit a model that fixes them (e.g., by adding "means" to the group.equal= argument) and use lavTestLRT() to compare model fit, just like equivalence of measurement parameters.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

parts:
Here is an example with the HZ example, for qualtile CI for alpha, Omega and AVE, for each factor




library(lavaan)
library(semTools)


## The famous Holzinger and Swineford (1939) example
HS.model <- ' visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6

speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '

fit <- cfa(HS.model, std.lv=T,
           data = HolzingerSwineford1939)
summary(fit, fit.measures = TRUE)

rels_fun <- function(obj){
  temp0 <- reliability(obj)
  temp <- c(temp0[1,], temp0[4,], temp0[5,])
  names(temp) <- c(paste0(c("alpha_"),
                          colnames(temp0)),
                   paste0(c("omega3_"),
                          colnames(temp0)),
                   paste0(c("ave_"),
                          colnames(temp0)))
  return(temp)  
}


bts <- bootstrapLavaan(fit, R=1000,
                       FUN=rels_fun,
                       type="ordinary")
bts
#### 95% quantile CI, and median
apply(bts, 2, function(x) quantile(x, c(.025, .5, .975)) )
